fences.title: construct not lowered
fences.why: A statement, expression, import, or definition has no lowering.
fences.fix: Rewrite it with the lowered constructs, as the hint for this fence says.

fences.title: annotation missing or not lowered
fences.why: A parameter, return, or variable needs an annotation the subset can read, or an annotation form has no more specific code.
fences.fix: Annotate the name with int, float, bool, str, bytes, list[T], dict[K, V], tuple[...], or a lowered class.

fences.title: generic alias annotation
fences.why: A subscripted annotation such as Mapping[K, V], Sequence[T], Iterator[T], Callable[...], or type[T] is not a lowered container.
fences.fix: Use list[T], dict[K, V], or tuple[...] in the signature.

fences.title: annotation names an unlowered type
fences.why: The annotation is a plain name that is not a builtin scalar, a lowered class, or a known alias.
fences.fix: Import a lowered class, or replace the alias with the concrete type.

fences.title: stdlib name not lowered
fences.why: The module imports, but this attribute is outside its lowered surface.
fences.fix: Use a lowered attribute of the module, or hand-write the logic.

fences.title: class body statement
fences.why: A class body holds only annotated fields without values and method definitions.
fences.fix: Move assignments into __init__ and declare fields with an annotation only.

fences.title: union annotation
fences.why: The IR has no tagged union yet, so `A | B` and `Union[A, B]` have no representation.
fences.fix: Narrow the annotation to one arm, or split the function per arm.

fences.title: call arguments not lowered
fences.why: A call has keyword arguments, or the wrong number of arguments, for its lowered form.
fences.fix: Pass positional arguments in the lowered arity.

fences.title: decorator
fences.why: Only a closed set of decorators lowers. Other decorators change behavior the compiler cannot see.
fences.fix: Remove the decorator, or inline what it does.

fences.title: dynamic or structural annotation
fences.why: object, Any, Protocol, TypeVar, Generic, Callable and ABC bases describe types the subset cannot represent natively.
fences.fix: Annotate with the concrete type the function really takes.

fences.title: Optional annotation
fences.why: An optional of one type (`T | None`, `Optional[T]`) is lowered. `A | B | None` and `Union[A, B, None]` need a multi-arm union, which the IR does not have yet.
fences.fix: Narrow to `T | None` with one arm, or split the function per arm.

fences.title: type mismatch
fences.why: An operation received a type the lowered subset does not accept for it.
fences.fix: Convert the operand explicitly, for example int(flag) before math calls.

fences.title: class header form
fences.why: Class keywords (metaclass=...) and multiple inheritance are not lowered.
fences.fix: Use a single lowered base class and no class keywords.

fences.title: forward reference annotation
fences.why: A quoted annotation such as 'Node' is not resolved by the lowering.
fences.fix: Define the class before use and write the name unquoted.

fences.title: operator or operand not lowered
fences.why: The operator is not lowered for these operand types.
fences.fix: Convert the operands to a supported pair of types.

fences.title: string literal outside Latin-1
fences.why: Strings are byte sequences in the runtime, so only Latin-1 text lowers.
fences.fix: Use Latin-1 text, or move the literal to bytes.

targets.label: Windows x86_64
targets.note: The compiler binary is built for Windows, but the emitted programs are not: the runtime needs POSIX headers the Win32 target does not provide. The Windows smoke never compiles or runs a program. There is no native Windows compile.

targets.label: WebAssembly (WASI preview1)
targets.note: A WASI preview1 command module. No subprocess, no dlopen and therefore no mix seam, no island fallback, and a preopen-only filesystem. The smoke lane proves stdout byte-identical to the native binary on the same program.

divergences.text: `int` is `i64`. Overflow aborts the process instead of growing a big int.
`//` by zero aborts the process instead of raising `ZeroDivisionError`.
Strings are a Latin-1 byte model. A string literal outside Latin-1 is a fence, and `unicodedata` covers only Latin-1 code points. A normalization that would leave Latin-1 raises `ValueError`.
divergences.note: the `unicodedata` row of the generated [supported](https://github.com/sigilco/pyscriptc/blob/master/.agents/docs/support/supported.md) table.

divergences.text: `re` is the runtime's byte-oriented backtracking subset, not CPython's `re`. `L`, `T`, `DEBUG` and unknown flag bits raise `ValueError`, `A` and `U` are no-ops, and a pattern that can loop without consuming stops with `RuntimeError` once its fuel is spent. Five or more groups are refused.
divergences.note: header of `src/pyscriptc/runtime/ps_re.c`, `re` row of the generated [supported](https://github.com/sigilco/pyscriptc/blob/master/.agents/docs/support/supported.md) table.

divergences.text: Set and `frozenset` iteration is insertion order, not CPython's hash order. Length and membership match.
After `for i in range(0)`, a new loop target reads as `0` instead of raising `UnboundLocalError`.
A subclass `__init__` that never assigns an inherited field leaves it at the zero value of its type instead of raising `AttributeError`.
`raise AppError("no")` for a user exception class stores a code and an optional `str` and does not call `__init__`.
`@classmethod` and `@staticmethod` of the form `Class.method(...)` do not pass the class object.

Some library failures surface as a different exception type: `importlib.resources.files` on a zip or missing package raises `ValueError` rather than `ModuleNotFoundError`, `shutil.copyfile` of the same path raises `RuntimeError` rather than `SameFileError`, other `shutil` and `os` failures are `RuntimeError`, and type errors on `unicodedata` calls surface as `ValueError`.
divergences.note: the `unicodedata` and `importlib.resources` rows of the generated [supported](https://github.com/sigilco/pyscriptc/blob/master/.agents/docs/support/supported.md) table.

divergences.text: `assert` is always evaluated; a compiled binary has no `-O`.
`x is None` lowers as `==` against `None`. Identical for `None` because it is a singleton; every other `is` on a scalar is refused.
`ABC`, `ABCMeta`, `Protocol`, `@abstractmethod` and `@overload` lower as plain classes and methods with no CPython runtime semantics.
Island calls (`subprocess.check_output`, `socket.gethostname`, `threading`, `logging`) run in an embedded CPython, so those follow the interpreter the binary links, not the pin.

`dotenv` lowers a closed subset of python-dotenv's parsing rules, and it differs from the library in three places. The subset: a UTF-8 BOM is stripped, blank lines and whole-line comments are skipped, an `export ` prefix is allowed, keys are bare (`KEY` alone binds `None`), an unquoted value runs to the end of the line with the ` #` comment cut and the rest right-stripped, a double-quoted value decodes `\" \\' \\ \a \b \f \n \r \t \v` and a single-quoted one only `\\` and `\'`, and a later binding overwrites an earlier one. No interpolation (`$NAME` stays literal), no multi-line values, no quoted keys, and the `stream`, `verbose`, `interpolate`, `override` and `encoding` arguments are fenced. The three differences: a malformed line raises `ValueError` where python-dotenv skips it with a warning, a missing file parses as the empty document where python-dotenv searches with `find_dotenv()`, and `load_dotenv` does not overwrite a variable that is already in the environment (its `override=False` default) while still returning `True` for a document with bindings.
divergences.note: header of `src/pyscriptc/runtime/ps_dotenv.c`, `dotenv` row of the generated [supported](https://github.com/sigilco/pyscriptc/blob/master/.agents/docs/support/supported.md) table.

divergences.text: `yaml.safe_load` covers a closed YAML subset, not all of PyYAML: timestamps and sexagesimal numbers (`1:30`) raise `ValueError` where PyYAML resolves them to `date` and `int` objects, and errors surface as `ValueError` rather than `yaml.YAMLError`.
divergences.note: header of `src/pyscriptc/runtime/ps_yaml.c`, `yaml` row of the generated [supported](https://github.com/sigilco/pyscriptc/blob/master/.agents/docs/support/supported.md) table.

divergences.text: HTTP and HTTPS go through a `curl` subprocess bridge, so the request is made by the host `curl` and depends on `curl` being on `PATH` at run time; a host without `curl` cannot make the call. The bridge needs the libpython-linked island shape, holds the whole body in memory with no streaming, and its TLS, proxy and redirect behavior is `curl`'s rather than CPython's.
